ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - reserved-pool-resv-prod-3 reports sustained 100% GPU utilization and queue length > 1200 for 6m. severity: P1. paging oncall.
maria (SRE): I'm on it, grabbing metrics. can someone start a quick bridge? :phone:
jordan (oncall): dialing 3rd-party bridge now. joining in 30s. @sam can you check autoscaler logs and quota? sam (infra): seeing autoscaler hitting API quota errors, cloud API 429s and then backoff. also a couple of failed launches due to ENI limit on the VPC.
lee (eng-runtime): confirmed model servers can't spin up new workers because the cluster autoscaler is receiving 429 from cloud provider and eventually gives up. logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:01Z autoscaler error: rate limited calling CreateInstance: Status 429
2026-03-15T03:12:45Z autoscaler: backoff exceeded, aborting scale-up attempt for pool resv-prod-3
```
anika (support): we're getting customer alerts from AcmeCorp and ZephyrPay about increased latency and 503s. AcmeCorp has reserved capacity there.
maria (SRE): customer impact confirmed: dedicated reservations in that pool are queued and being throttled. need immediate live mitigations: 1) reduce noisy low-priority sessions 2) fail-open some reservations to alternate pools 3) manual eviction of best-effort tasks.
jordan (oncall): bridge up: https://company-bridge/6112223334  - added SRE + infra + runtime + support
sam (infra): quick action: bumping cloud API rate limits isn't possible mid-incident. we can pause non-critical provisioning and kick any queued warmup jobs. starting evict script for best-effort actors.
sam (infra): running:
```
./scripts/evict-best-effort.sh --pool resv-prod-3 --threshold 0.8
```
ops-bot: evict-best-effort job started, 74 best-effort sessions targeted.
lee (eng-runtime): pushing a routing override to route reserved tenants with SLA to resv-prod-1 (same region) where we have headroom. command:
```
redwood route set --tenant acmecorp --pool resv-prod-1 --ttl 600
```
maria (SRE): doing controlled reroutes only for enterprise tenants. can we ensure model variant compatibility? lee: yes, resv-prod-1 runs same model family and we have fallback quantized variants for burst.
anika (support): messaging update to AcmeCorp: "We're seeing capacity pressure in your reserved pool, routing some traffic to a warm fallback pool to maintain latency. will follow up with RCA." sending now.
jordan (oncall): oncall checklist: 1) reduce queue pressure 2) enable burst routing 3) monitor tail latency 4) open support updates - done/doing.
sam (infra): autoscaler publish rate now limited but I can manually request a scale-up using provider console for 6 extra GPUs as emergency capacity. requesting approval from infra lead.
maria (SRE): grant emergency if it helps. do it and we can drain traffic back.
sam (infra): cloud console request submitted, provider accepted 4 GPUs (ENI limit prevented full request). provisioning in progress.
ops-bot: provider-event: 4 instances provisioning for resv-prod-3, expected ready in ~90s.
lee (eng-runtime): while we wait, enabling aggressive KV prefix caching and increasing batch window to reduce per-token cost and throughput. config snippet:
```
runtime.config.batch_window_ms = 30 -> 100
runtime.cache.enabled = true
```
maria (SRE): also enabling reservation-burst fallback policy to allow reserved tenants to use compatible capacity in resv-prod-1/resv-prod-2.
anika (support): AcmeCorp responded: "Thanks for the fast mitigation. We're seeing errors drop but some jobs still queued." will escalate if they see degraded quality.
jordan (oncall): monitoring dashboard: queue depth trending down from 1.2k -> 380 over 6m after evictions + reroute + cache.
sam (infra): instances are ready and registered. autoscaler resumed but still throttled for a bit. watch for duplicate spin-ups.
lee (eng-runtime): verifying worker health: all new nodes have runtime 2.8.1 and quantized kernel present. OK.
maria (SRE): can we capture why ENI limit occurred? looks like a stale subnet allocation from recent canary. sam: investigating.
sam (infra): root cause hypothesis: a recent canary test created a large number of ephemeral NICs in that subnet and didn't tear down due to bug. filing infra ticket to clean up.
jordan (oncall): customer bridge summary: AcmeCorp and ZephyrPay impacted with increased latencies and temporary 503s; rerouted critical traffic, evicted best-effort, manually added 4 GPUs, and enabled fallback pools. impact window ~03:12 - 03:24 UTC. oncall will follow up with timeline and postmortem.
anika (support): I'll send updated customer note with ETA for full recovery and offer to join any customer calls.
maria (SRE): action items for post-incident: 1) autoscaler resiliency: handle 429s gracefully with retry jitter and a queued fallback 2) runbook update: include manual provisioning steps and burst routing SOP 3) subnet/ENI cleanup to prevent future quota blocks 4) add proactive alert when ENI/utilization > 80% for reserved pools.
lee (eng-runtime): also add a runtime knob to immediately reduce batch-window when queue spike detected to trade cost for latency faster.
sam (infra): creating infra ticket INF-4729 for ENI cleanup and quota increase request; adding timeline.
ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED - capacity restored and queue under acceptable thresholds. severity will be downgraded pending RCA.
maria (SRE): thanks team. follow-ups: assign owners and schedule RCA meeting. I'll own the runbook updates. jordan, can you own the customer post-incident note with timestamps? jordan (oncall): yes, I'll draft and send in 30m.
anika (support): adding support ticket updates and linking to bridge notes.
maria (SRE): short notes for RCA:
- initial trigger: autoscaler hit cloud API 429s + ENI quota interfering with scale-up
- contributing: noisy ephemeral NICs from canary not torn down
- mitigations: best-effort eviction, reroute reserved tenants, manual provisioning, runtime caching and batch-window adjustments
- next: infra quota cleanup, autoscaler retry improvements, runbook updates
maria (SRE): closing thread here, moving full log to incidents/bridge/6112223334 for the RCA doc. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
